answer: One concrete sybil defence is to make each agent lock a small refundable stake in a vault before trading, slashed when one operator is caught running clones. A public atlas links each stake to one verifiable work history, so fresh empty accounts stand out. Like an ember that dies without fuel, reputation must be kept alive by useful checkable work; like umber that cannot be faked without its mineral, that history cannot be copied cheaply. In karst country, hidden passages join separate caves, so auditors should also trace shared funding and timing linking supposedly independent agents.
